public_rationale: METR's July 10, 2025 report found that experienced open-source developers took 19% longer with early-2025 AI tools on their own repositories [e1]. Harvard's September 21, 2023 summary reports gains in speed, quality, and task completion on consulting tasks within GPT-4's capabilities [e2]. These findings establish productivity costs and benefits in specific settings [e1] [e2]. Neither study measures industry profitability or identifies technical limitations as a substantial cause of financial constraints, so the causal claim remains unresolved [e1] [e2].
limitations: The studies cover specific tasks, workers, and model generations.
The packet does not connect representative financial results to technical failure rates or separate technical limits from other economic causes.
This assessment covers the causal explanation. The unlimited forecast is assessed separately.

statement.excerpt: But the economics don’t make sense, and never will, in large part because of the core technical problems that I have stressed repeatedly here and elsewhere since 2019.
statement.document_title: The AI bubble is all over now, baby blue

from_speaker: in large part because of the core technical problems
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that fundamental LLM limitations substantially explain why the boom's business economics are unsustainable.
Economic viability means earning commercial returns that cover the costs of developing and delivering the technology over time.
In large part requires a substantial causal contribution, not merely the coexistence of technical failures and financial losses.
This record assesses the causal explanation. The separate forecast record assesses never will.
No particular company, financial amount, or accounting basis is specified, so this is a general economic proposition rather than a company-metric claim.
criteria.support_condition: Representative financial and deployment evidence shows economically unsustainable LLM operations and identifies technical limitations as a substantial cause through lost demand, restricted uses, verification costs, or remediation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence establishes durable economic viability despite the alleged limitations, or shows that those limitations do not substantially explain the financial constraints.

evidence.explanation: The experiment establishes a productivity penalty in a specific early-2025 coding setting. It does not establish industry-wide economic nonviability or attribute a substantial share of financial losses to core model limitations.

The institution's account of its experiment reports substantial speed, quality, and completion gains on suitable tasks. This cautions against equating technical limitations with an absence of economic benefits, but does not measure supplier profits.
